title: Weight-Space Programming for Medical Imaging: Do We Still Need Training Data?
why_wsp: Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra each write every weight of a small LeNet-style CNN from a natural-language task description in a single tool-free reply, with no images or training.
domain: medical image classification (chest X-ray, breast ultrasound, abdominal CT from MedMNIST; pelvic MRI SynthUterus)
editor: Claude Opus 5.5 (Claude Code 2.1.319 headless) and GPT-6 Astra (OpenAI Responses API), reasoning effort high
target: ProgNet, a one-stage LeNet-style CNN, 591 to 6,974 parameters per task
self_editing: no; LLM writes a separate small CNN from scratch
fraction_or_count_of_weights_changed: all weights written from zero; "22-94% of their weights are exactly zero, and each network uses only 8-145 distinct values" (Opus; Sec 4.2)

headline_results.claim: Above chance on all six MedMNIST tasks
headline_results.quote: The LLM-written networks perform above chance on all six MedMNIST tasks, with a mean test AUC of 0.719 for Opus and 0.711 for Astra.

headline_results.claim: Beat zero-shot MedSigLIP on 5 of 6 tasks
headline_results.quote: Both models outperform MedSigLIP on 5 of 6 tasks while using more than 10^4 times fewer parameters.

headline_results.claim: Adam on 256 labels beats LLM-written nets on every MedMNIST task
headline_results.quote: the same network trained with Adam on only 256 labelled images achieves a higher AUC on every MedMNIST task (mean AUC 0.828)
On SynthUterus, Opus attains an AUC of 0.764, whereas Astra falls below chance (AUC 0.136) owing to a systematic error.
ChestMNIST, the mean AUC over 14 findings, stays close to chance (0.552).

cost.quote: 128k output tokens including reasoning; answers take up to 79k

baselines_and_controls: zero-shot MedSigLIP-448; same ProgNet trained with Adam on 256 labels and on full data; published ResNet-18 for reference; low-exposure dataset (SynthUterus) as contamination control
runs_and_variance: three independent calls per LLM per task, mean +/- sd reported; quote: "Results were consistent across the three independent calls, with the largest variation on BreastMNIST for Astra (0.067)." (Sec 4.1)
memorization_vs_reasoning: LLMs set output biases from unstated MedMNIST class priors they quote correctly (e.g. "About 73% of BreastMNIST images are label 1"; true 73.1%), while all SynthUterus biases were zero; authors state they cannot separate how much MedMNIST performance rests on dataset knowledge.
limitations_stated: 28x28 images and <=7k-weight networks; MedSigLIP handicapped by upsampled inputs and untuned prompts; SynthUterus small, synthetic, recent; two LLMs, one prompt; prompt did not describe image layout; MedMNIST contamination cannot be excluded.
cites_or_builds_on: csinva weight-space programming from scratch on simple tasks (report, 2026-11-02)
notes_for_survey: Tests B2 writing in a domain with no source code for the rules; written networks beat a zero-shot VLM on 5/6 tasks but lose to 256-label training on all. Includes a weight-level comparison (sparse, few distinct values, textbook filters) and a low-exposure dataset where one writer inverted the classes from a layout assumption.
